questions.question_text:
For some value of $x$ in $-1\le x\le 1$, $\sin\left(\arccos x\right)=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$ and $\tan\left(\arccos x\right)<0$.
Find the exact value of $x$.

options.why: Solved for $x^{2}$ correctly but ignored the condition $\tan\left(\arccos x\right)<0$, which forces quadrant 2 and so $x<0$.
Read $\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$ as the value of $x$ itself rather than as the opposite over the hypotenuse.
Took $\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$ as $x$ and also ignored the sign condition.

questions.solution_text:
$\sin\left(\arccos x\right)=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$
$\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$
$1-x^{2}=\frac{7}{16}$
$x^{2}=\frac{9}{16}$
$x=\pm\frac{3}{4}$
$\tan\left(\arccos x\right)<0$ places $\arccos x$ in quadrant 2, so $x<0$.
$x=-\frac{3}{4}$
